reviews.text: The 355 is a mix of great elements from great spy movies, coupled with a great cast – creating a product that is significantly less than the sum of its parts.
reviews.author: Justin Kim

reviews.text: “The 355” has an “Ocean’s Eight” vibe (2018) in that it cares more about women linking up more than the actual story when it should not have to be a choice.
reviews.author: Sarah Vincent

reviews.text:
The 355 left me frustrated and disappointed 
A great concept 
An excellent cast 
& terrible pacing, execution, & even one note characters.
reviews.author: Zach Pope

reviews.text: While The 355 certainly does not bring anything electrifying to the action genre, there is something wonderful about seeing an action movie led by five women who are 38 years old or older.
reviews.author: Tina Kakadelis

reviews.text: Here’s the 411 on The 355 — it’s a bloated bore.
reviews.author: M.N. Miller

reviews.text: The 355 could've been a much better spy thriller under a more capable director, but the kick-ass, highly-capable female cast saves the movie and made this an enjoyable action movie.
reviews.author: Ruth Maramis

reviews.text: “The 355” won’t exactly stick with you long after seeing it, nor is it the kind of movie that will wow you with its originality and vision. But it is light and breezy entertainment that happily wears its influences on it’s sleeve.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: Oh-so-basic with its killer lady spies, their battle against misogyny and their quest to claim some much-needed on-screen space.
reviews.author: Sarah Ward

reviews.text: A rehash of countless similar films, just as mediocre or insufferable, but here male camaraderie is replaced by female complicity. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Javier Ocaña

reviews.text: In this tangle of platitudes, feminist discourses, and vertiginous persecutions, the film is nothing more than a clumsy reflection of what it wants to enfranchise itself from. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Paula Vázquez Prieto

reviews.text:
Offers no great surprises. 
[Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: The fact that the end product of this dream team-up is so bland and uninspired makes it feel that much more disappointing.
reviews.author: Dan Bayer

reviews.text:
So if most of the cast delivers, what's the problem? Clues point to Kinberg and Theresa Rebeck's script. It throws around terms like "brush pass" and "kill box," but also gives us dialogue like this:
"A man must cover his tracks."
"Yes he does."
...what?
reviews.author: Pete Vonder Haar

reviews.text: This film is an exercise in formula with an eye to setting up sequels, and the main reason it works as well as it does is the chemistry between the lead players.
reviews.author: A.C. Koch

reviews.text: Aggressively average.
reviews.author: Matt Brunson

reviews.text: The 355 boasts an incredible cast of powerhouse actresses from around the world, who are given a bland, formulaic script unbefitting of their talent.
reviews.author: Rachel Ho

reviews.text: What The 355 offers up is a perfect Saturday afternoon dad movie, but instead of starring Stallone or Eastwood or Bronson, it stars five women with six Oscar nominations and two wins between them. (And was written by the creator of NBCs Smash!)
reviews.author: Liz Shannon Miller

reviews.text: ...the arms-length atmosphere compounded by a continuing emphasis on ineffective, lackluster set-pieces...
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: This movie might have an incredible cast, but that doesnt save it from being completely mediocre, very forgettable, and honestly, a bit dull.
reviews.author: Tessa Smith

reviews.text: The main problem is that Kinberg, a better screenwriter and producer than director, hired award-caliber actors to play low-grade roles. It didn't work.
reviews.author: Dan Buffa

reviews.text: Despite the amazing work of its cast, this espionage saga lacks thrills and originality. Full Review in Spanish
reviews.author: Rene Sanchez

reviews.text: The movie has all the potential of being unchallenging escapist entertainment, but it's all too familiar to distinguish itself.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: Unfortunately, despite how much I wanted to like The 355 and for how many reasons, it is a poor film.
reviews.author: Carey-Ann Pawsey

reviews.text: The 355 is overplotted but underwritten, a globetrotting chase flick with plenty of halfway-decent action sequences but minimal reasons for us to care about the characters’ fates.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: falls short of providing a genuine alternative to the traditional male-driven action thriller.
reviews.author: Eddie Harrison

reviews.text: ...A mess of convoluted plot twists and airport-novel contrivances...
reviews.author: Clint Worthington

reviews.text: So much great talent in this film that was wasted not put to good use. There's too much running around instead of getting straight to the point.
reviews.author: Brandon Avery

reviews.text: It’s the sort of thing best enjoyed with some snarky friends and a couple of bottles of wine.
reviews.author: Eleanor Ringel Cater

reviews.text: Undone by a wholehearted embrace of all of the worst action-adventure filmmaking techniques of the past two decades.
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: Some of the action sequences were cringy.
reviews.author: Tony Baker

reviews.text: Charlie's Angels on steroids -- female power all the way.
reviews.author: Jackie K. Cooper

reviews.text: Even with all the boxes checked, The 355 is not the full-on all-female actioner it hopes to be. There is a lot of talent here, maybe too much for a lesser film like this.
reviews.author: Thom Ernst

reviews.text: [A] same-old-same-old action antique, a movie whose every beat rings familiar. We could have gotten something new with this one. Instead, we've seen it all before.
reviews.author: Allen Adams

reviews.text: he main problem, besides the awful dialogue, is with the movie's austere tone. It needed to be much lighter.
reviews.author: Chad Byrnes

reviews.text: This all-female spy thriller is not the representation we asked for.
reviews.author: Katey Stoetzel

reviews.text: The 355 is an entertaining if unremarkable spy movie, with predictable story beats and mediocre action that's only somewhat saved by its strong cast.
reviews.author: Molly Freeman

reviews.text: "The 355" requires a filmmaker with an eye for choreography and urgency, which is lacking in almost every frame in his latest.
reviews.author: Matthew Passantino

reviews.text: The 355 is, at best, passable.
reviews.author: Travis Johnson

reviews.text: There's no world in which the picture would have been a success.
reviews.author: Walter Chaw

reviews.text: What follows, it is true, has been seen a thousand times before. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ezequiel Boetti

reviews.text: This 124-minute movie is fast-paced, well-acted and asks some interesting questions about where one’s loyalty lies.
reviews.author: Stephen Romei

reviews.text: Only intermittently engaging; lacks the pacing, deftness and wit to mask all the cliches that we're so familiar with by now.
reviews.author: Peter Canavese

reviews.text: A disastrously ill-made collection of some of the most illegible action scenes that a film with a budget of not less than $40 million could conceivably possess.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: It's a Bond wannabe that has the audacity to mention Bond in its dialogue.
reviews.author: Linda Cook

reviews.text: "The 355," a feminist spin on James Bond movies, is undone by plot holes, a herky-jerky pace and inconsistent tone.
reviews.author: Russ Simmons

reviews.text: Here we have an action movie about jet-setting spies played by huge stars in which the fate of the world hangs in the balance and, yet, The 355's pulse never seems to raise above resting rate.
reviews.author: David Bax

reviews.text: This simplistic approach, which forces an evil/ethical binary, paired with a ham-fisted dialogue, flattens the film and makes the lulls between fight scenes feel more like retribution than respite.
reviews.author: Becca James

reviews.text: Next week, I will have forgotten that I ever saw this movie and will be ever so slightly happier for it, though I will not recall why. But I will be happier.
reviews.author: Ciara Wardlow

reviews.text: At more than two hours long, and with so many logistical flaws, emotional misses, and really, a missed purpose, The 355 blows its cover.
reviews.author: Frank Wilkins

reviews.text: Despite its plethora of gaping plot inconsistencies, and an all-too obvious ode to the united colors of Benetton-approach to global spy configurations, there's something working here that still feels worth watching.
reviews.author: Piers Marchant

reviews.text: A textbook example of the kind of film you find playing to empty theaters during the midwinter doldrums.
reviews.author: Sean Burns

reviews.text: Eight minutes in and it was hard to believe this was even going into theaters. Two hours later it was an instant candidate for one of the laziest thrillers to be released throughout 2022.
reviews.author: Erik Childress

reviews.text: It's too silly to take itself as seriously as it does. Not even actors this talented can sell some of the dialogue they're asked to deliver with straight faces.
reviews.author: Mark Meszoros

reviews.text: If you've ever seen a mediocre action movie with a surprisingly stacked cast, then you've basically seen this.
reviews.author: Kristy Puchko

reviews.text: An easier film to like it for what it is rather than what it isn't, [Simon] Kinberg's created enough of an escape here that undemanding audiences are likely to enjoy the global trottings of these capable, captivating women.
reviews.author: Peter Gray

reviews.text: Thewomen are having such a good time kicking butt and getting names that it's a shame thattheformulaic plot devices slow it down.
reviews.author: Lynn Venhaus

reviews.text: A nondescript action thriller that will be easily and swiftly forgotten.
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: The quintette, as likable as they are, face even bigger challenges in the flat script and clunky action choreography that undercuts their collective energy.
reviews.author: Tom Meek

reviews.text: It was fine, but there are so many spy thriller movies, espionage movies, heist movies out there that are so much more than just fine.
reviews.author: Jeremy Jahns

reviews.text: Looking cool and acting tough isn't enough, which The 355 fails to understand.
reviews.author: Nick Johnston

reviews.text: There is plenty to indicate that the story's breathless Around The World In 80 Days tone is deliberately tongue-in-cheek, but the directorial mishandling makes it feel off-puttingly repetitive.
reviews.author: John Lui

reviews.text: A star-studded espionage romp that delivers a high-kicking, sharp-shooting, jet-setting, and impeccably turned-out fight against the forces of overwhelming global demise.
reviews.author: Hilary A White

reviews.text: The high-powered cast is more than up for it, adding warmth and humour at every turn. So it's increasingly frustrating that the movie is so sloppy and unintentionally silly.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: There's nothing here that Angelina Jolie and Scarlett Johansson haven't done already but Kinberg and his nimble cast achieve such momentum that you'll probably shelve your reservations until it's all over.
reviews.author: Sandra Hall

reviews.text: Doggedly mediocre actioner The 355 is the cinematic equivalent of gathering together Formula 1's finest drivers and tossing them the keys to a Yugo.
reviews.author: Kimberley Jones

reviews.text: The abundance of female beauty will cause hetero cisgender men such as myself, with enough male toxicity to enjoy football and gun-shooting spies to be captivated enough to dismiss the boredom gathering like lint at the edges of our consciousnesses.
reviews.author: Mark Jackson

reviews.text: The nicest thing I can say is it reminded me of a very funny scene in another movie.
reviews.author: Chase Hutchinson

reviews.text: A star-studded, action-packed extravaganza.
reviews.author: Shawn Edwards

reviews.text: While rarely dreadful, The 355 is the type of disposable shlock destined to become a forgettable January footnote.
reviews.author: Matt Conway

reviews.text: The 355 is a spy thriller that has all the makings of a great action comedy. Instead it presents total absurdity and clichés with a straight face.
reviews.author: Alci Rengifo

reviews.text: An unimaginative thriller that wastes its star talents on a bland script, mediocre action, and underbaked themes.
reviews.author: Jonathan Sim

reviews.text: I think there may have been an attempt to keep this as real and grounded as possible, but the spy genre allows for some creativity in the storytelling and characters. We can bend reality a bit if we're constantly having fun and kept on our toes.
reviews.author: Paul McGuire Grimes

reviews.text: Belongs in the deep trenches of the Netflix algorithm along with other basic spy flicks that feel as if they were made by bots.
reviews.author: Rendy Jones

reviews.text: ...as films like Mission: Impossible have shown us, a simple plot like this can be elevated through amazing action sequences and memorable characters. The 355 has neither.
reviews.author: Natasha Alvar

reviews.text: This cool spy/action thriller is elevated by an awesome all-female cast and by the fact that the story gives you a peek into each character's personal life. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fico Cangiano

reviews.text: A lack of intrigue dooms the movie from the get-go.
reviews.author: Dana Barbuto

reviews.text: [An] often generic but surprisingly engaging espionage action/thriller.
reviews.author: Dwight Brown

reviews.text: The pulchritudinous cast help this OK popcorn pusher hang together well enough. It's no classic, but at least it's no Ocean's 8.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: This is a title that screams, "Watch me at home!"
reviews.author: Sara Michelle Fetters

reviews.text: Feels like a film destined to be forgotten, relegated to late night showings on basic cable, while the cast (without exception better than the material they're given) moves on to bigger and better things.
reviews.author: Mattie Lucas

reviews.text: The piling of event upon event and character upon character makes it difficult to connect with any of the protagonists.
reviews.author: Noah Berlatsky

reviews.text: January is here.
reviews.author: Matthew Razak

reviews.text: Diane Kruger slapping Jessica Chastain across the face with a frozen fish should be funny.
reviews.author: Simran Hans

reviews.text: Its dullness somehow feels worse than grand failure, as though its aims were only to prove that a bunch of the most famous women on Earth can come together to make an action film just as uninspired and boring as men can.
reviews.author: Alison Willmore

reviews.text: The 355 boasts exactly one genuinely suspenseful scene (it happens around the 3/4 point) but that lasts only about five minutes and therefore represents less than 5% of the overall running time.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: It's a diverting but ham-fisted attempt at Mission: Impossible-style antics.
reviews.author: Edward Porter

reviews.text: Not so much old-school as out-of-date.
reviews.author: Matthew Bond

reviews.text: The 355 is an average American action flick that has all the highs of spy thrillers and all the woes that come with an action ensemble cast and a heavy hand.
reviews.author: Kate Sánchez

reviews.text: The 355 is bland, poorly shot, and somewhat lifeless. It is a shame because the cast is great, but their characters aren't compelling enough to make the film any less dull.
reviews.author: Austin Burke

reviews.text: The top-notch female cast isn't provided a decent blueprint to develop out of the provided stereotypes. The James Bond-Mission: Impossible spin that the actors try to emulate never takes full flight.
reviews.author: Elias Savada

reviews.text: This predictable and nearly emotionless spy flick has neither charismatic characters (despite a recognizable and talented cast) nor any memorable action.
reviews.author: Nicolás Delgadillo

reviews.text: There's a lot of fun to be had with this all-action film starring a powerful cast - even if the nature of an origin story dulls the impact somewhat.
reviews.author: Lisa Giles-Keddie

reviews.text: The 355" is one of the ugliest, most visually incoherent entries in the genre in years.
reviews.author: Dominic Griffin

reviews.text: Striving to be mentioned in the same breath as Bond or Bourne, The 355 makes a major flaw in assuming its audience is unperturbed by a nonsense plot...The leads are too good for this suffocating killjoy parading as a serious action thriller.
reviews.author: Candice McMillan

reviews.text: Slick but empty spy B-film.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: It has everything you could want out of a spy thriller, with some of the best women in the business kicking ass.
reviews.author: Sara Clements

reviews.text: It runs a little bit long, and it's overly predictable at times... but it's better than some crappy found footage horror movie, which we always get in January.
reviews.author: Kevin Carr

reviews.text: Jessica Chastain, Lupita Nyong'o, Penelope Cruz among the great talents insulting the audience's intelligence.
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: A well-produced, shallow B-movie that's too monotonous, unimaginative and dull to be fun or thrilling, despite a great cast.
reviews.author: Avi Offer

reviews.text: If by some miracle, there's a second helping of this uninspired brew, a title already awaits. How about The 356?
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: It is pure catnip for fans of the genre of beautiful women fighting off the bad guys with aplomb
reviews.author: Gary M. Kramer

reviews.text: The 355 is an apt description of how many seconds it takes before the sheer weight of missed opportunities sinks in.
reviews.author: Cain Noble-Davies

reviews.text: The plot was incredibly thin and I thought the script should have been more developed.
reviews.author: Lael Loewenstein

reviews.text: If only the film The 355 were as ambitious and filled with the same outside-the-box thinking as this rockin' team made up of some of the finest actresses working today.
reviews.author: Steven Prokopy

reviews.text: These women are dazzling and working so hard in such a derivative secret agent actioner.
reviews.author: Tim Cogshell

reviews.text: The tony likes of Jessica Chastain, Penelope Cruz, Lupita Nyong'o, and Diane Kruger seem lost amongst the multitude of adventure film cliches, flat dialogue, and over-edited action scenes.
reviews.author: Jeff York

reviews.text: It plays like a press conference made uninteresting flesh. No sooner endured than forgotten.
reviews.author: Donald Clarke

reviews.text: It's to the credit of the cast that The 355 still keeps its head above water in spite of the sputtering finale.
reviews.author: Sean Collier

reviews.text: Many will take this as a sign that women don't sell action movies. Actually, bad action movies don't sell action movies and Hollywood owes its female stars better than this.
reviews.author: Dan Murrell

reviews.text: This twisty, suspenseful actioner is remarkably strong, kicking over stereotypes with its team of international secret agents who are powerful, smart, and could go toe to toe with James Bond.
reviews.author: Tara McNamara

reviews.text: If you're looking for something simple, fun, well-paced and with just enough substance to keep you satisfied for the full two hours, The 355 is your number one.
reviews.author: Gemma Creagh

reviews.text: Some of the action pieces are energetic enough to trick you into thinking there's substance to the story, but it's clear by the second act that this is an empty op.
reviews.author: Matt Fowler

reviews.text: Yes, Chastain makes for a kinetic action hero, as do a few of her co-stars, and she's someone who most assuredly puts her money where her mouth is. But no, this is not the all-female Bond franchise you're looking for.
reviews.author: David Fear

reviews.text: This is thankfully not as shallow an enterprise as say, Charlie's Angels, but the potential was there for so much more. Still, there is fun to be had if you check your brain at the box office.
reviews.author: Pete Hammond

reviews.text: Unfortunately, all of that talent is wasted on a poorly written script that succumbs to the genre's many tropes. It all unfolds in a disappointing and predictable manner.
reviews.author: Micheal Compton

reviews.text: Cruz does her best with an underwritten character in a film that might have done more to rise above its noble concept, but is thoroughly watchable nonetheless.
reviews.author: Paul Whitington

reviews.text: "The 355" is an instantly unmemorable spy-thriller that forgets to have fun with its ludicrous premise.
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: As a gender-reversed variation on the sort of high-tech globetrotting spy saga we've seen before, the ambition of this stylish yet formulaic potboiler outshines the execution.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: This film definitely needed a better script to glue the predictable action together, but Chastain, Kruger, Nyong'o and Cruz kick butt together well, proving that besides being easy on the eyes, they're plenty rough around the edges.
reviews.author: Linda and Al Lerner

reviews.text: It's hard to not laugh out loud at some of the cheesy dialogue as well, as lines like "Because we're spies, asshole" only enhance its spoof-like qualities. If only it were a spoof.
reviews.author: Catherine Springer

reviews.text: It's the gals kicking booty, why no script adjustment for gender to make it more interesting? Who makes them feel like Natural Women? Smith & Wesson, sadly, Smith & Wesson.
reviews.author: Patrick McDonald

reviews.text: Mostly, The 355 succeeds where others have come up short because it put the movie and the story first -- not the message.
reviews.author: Lindsey Bahr

reviews.text: Chastain, Kruger, Nyong'o, Cruz, and Bingbing are a force to be reckoned with although they're no match for the bad script.
reviews.author: Joe Friar

reviews.text: "The 355" devolves into a bullet-spattered endurance test.
reviews.author: Ty Burr

reviews.text: Doesn't add up.
reviews.author: Nate Adams

reviews.text: The 355 features a messy, overly convoluted and too-long plot that often leaves its talented multi-national actors with little to do except run and shoot and look glamorously injured.
reviews.author: Chris Knight

reviews.text: Sometimes a well executed formula can be a relief. The women are beautiful and smart, they're no airheads and there's nothing campy about them, which is also a relief.
reviews.author: Roger Friedman

reviews.text: The 355 is not only wasting the time of it's all-star cast but halfway through we realize it's wasting our time as well.
reviews.author: Leo Brady

reviews.text: Unless someone plans on putting out a documentary featuring the slow and methodical burning of the missing reels of The Magnificent Ambersons, I cannot easily imagine a greater and more pointless squandering than this.
reviews.author: Peter Sobczynski

reviews.text: A stellar cast of five cannot overcome three fatal flaws: repetition, lack of originality, and predictability
reviews.author: J. Don Birnam

reviews.text: Name any twist or trick you've seen via misdirection, switching sides, or tenuous allyship while in the foxhole and The 355 has it. This doesn't mean that the film isn't entertaining, it's that... it falls back on what audiences know.
reviews.author: Douglas Davidson

reviews.text: Desperately in need of a better script and characters, the talented cast can do only so much with the material given to them. Maybe the 355 refers to the collective number of times they asked, "Is this all there is?"
reviews.author: Jim Judy

reviews.text: ...we need more female-led action films, but The 355 is not worthy of the all-star cast of women it has assembled.
reviews.author: Tom Santilli

reviews.text: Like James Bond being tasked with filling out paperwork for HR, the actresses in "The 355" are sent on a mission they are clearly overqualified for.
reviews.author: Rob Thomas

reviews.text: [The 355 is] as hollow a tale of female empowerment as they come, thinking that simply placing a gun in the hands of its protagonists makes them feminist icons.
reviews.author: Steven Warner

reviews.text: Joins the ranks of recent action movies that follow all-too-familiar patterns and substitute mayhem for imagination and genuine excitement. And the fact that its kick-ass protagonists are women is no compensation.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: The 355 amasses some of the most talented and electrifying actresses in the world, then squanders them in a generic and forgettable action picture.
reviews.author: Christy Lemire

reviews.text: A star-studded, yet sloppily-executed spy/thriller that never quite delivers on its potential.
reviews.author: Kevin Brackett

reviews.text: The 355 may not be the most memorable espionage thriller, but it checks the boxes of what I want to see in a spy film, including a great cast and entertaining action scenes.
reviews.author: Lauren Bradshaw

reviews.text: If you can turn your brain off for two hours and cast the horrifying politics and Kinberg problems aside, The 355 is a pretty enjoyable and ridiculous popcorn flick.
reviews.author: Marina Ashioti

reviews.text: Take The 355 at face value and enjoy the ride. Kruger and Nyong'o elevate the material to a level it probably doesn't deserve with Chastain and Cruz following closely behind.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: Dull nearly to the point of indifference.
reviews.author: Kurt Loder

reviews.text: An ace ensemble is let down by subpar action and a rehashed story.
reviews.author: Chris Bumbray

reviews.text: The problem is that you can't have girl power if the girls aren't interesting. And trust me, these she-spies are anything but.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: While "The 355" isn't a bad film, it's just a disappointing and mediocre one considering all the talent on screen.
reviews.author: Cary Darling

reviews.text: This is a film that delivers the package with fire and flair...as long as you don't mind a few scorch marks or cracks on it when it arrives.
reviews.author: Johnny Gayzmonic

reviews.text: When it comes to The 355, the cast is willing but the script is weak.
reviews.author: Sherin Nicole

reviews.text: What a bummer to kick off 2022 at the movies with a lame, gender-flipped mission impossible. Chastain and her team of women warriors look ready to rip, so it's a shame that director Simon Kinberg traps them in an empty, soulless mess.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: Sure, spy-action movies are a particularly daft breed and suspending disbelief comes with the territory, but 'The 355' asks far too much for so little in return.
reviews.author: Brian Lloyd

reviews.text: After a bumpy start the film settles into a fast and feisty pace with incredible stunts and fight sequences.
reviews.author: Dulcie Pearce

reviews.text: The 355 feels like a missed opportunity.
reviews.author: Brian Viner

reviews.text: Rarely has a spy thriller so much resembled a pile of ironing.
reviews.author: Stephanie Zacharek

reviews.text: The 355 is good old action fun with a well-constructed story and better than all of the bad James Bond movies.
reviews.author: Alan Ng

reviews.text: A less predictable plot and more globe-trotting would have been more than enough to make this a special spy thriller.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Lyles

reviews.text: The powerhouse women in the movie are what make "The 355" a bearable watch, however, the story is forgettable and a missed opportunity with a talented cast.
reviews.author: Susan Kamyab

reviews.text: The film does what it advertises, but it leaves so much more on the table.
reviews.author: Allen Almachar

reviews.text: This film is simply mind-blowing -- for its waste of the viewer's time, but mostly for its waste of talent.
reviews.author: David Kaplan

reviews.text: It doesn't matter how exceptional the cast is if the screenplay is lousy.
reviews.author: Jeanne Kaplan

reviews.text: If the film leaned more into its feminine world to explore espionage through that lens, that would've been something, but there's no leaning into anything except for tired ideas and boring plot points.
reviews.author: Rob Dean

reviews.text: If you're hoping that The 355 will be will be a female empowerment action flick, you're going to be disappointed.
reviews.author: Richard Propes

reviews.text: Filled with one-dimensional heroes, predictable double-crosses and been-there-done-that action sequences, The 355 does not bring out the full potential of its stellar cast.
reviews.author: Laura Sirikul

reviews.text: Gives its stars almost nothing exciting or interesting to do, stranding them in a story recycled from dozens of other espionage thrillers.
reviews.author: Josh Bell

reviews.text: Cruz and Chastain team up to ruin their Oscar chances in this discardable action flick.
reviews.author: Dustin Chase

reviews.text: Much is lost and nothing gained, for all involved.
reviews.author: Christopher Llewellyn Reed

reviews.text: The 355 is far from great or worthwhile, but if it were a Netflix film, it would probably be in their Top 10 for at least three weeks, then rarely ever talked about again.
reviews.author: Jon Negroni

reviews.text: The movie seems so concerned with creating a thrilling and exciting atmosphere of globe-trotting action, and hard-charging energy, that it never once stops to consider whether it's actually thrilling or exciting (spoiler: its not).
reviews.author: Rodrigo Perez

reviews.text: It would be better, for all involved, unfortunately, if this ill-conceived movie was forgotten, too.
reviews.author: Robert Daniels

reviews.text: There isn't enough plot to flesh out the story, and there's way too much action to make the story watchable. The 355 isn't even dumb fun. It's exhausting noise considering the caliber of actors.
reviews.author: MontiLee Stormer

reviews.text: What was probably a well intentioned distaff take on the standard spy action picture feels more like an adequate throwback.
reviews.author: Joanna Langfield

reviews.text: The 355 stands out as - not a must-see - a may-as-well see...
reviews.author: Phil Villarreal

reviews.text: What fun to see women doing what their male counterparts have traditionally and cavalierly been doing for so long, barefoot or in heels.
reviews.author: Lisa Johnson Mandell

reviews.text: Double crosses and faked deaths are easier to spot than Waldo.
reviews.author: Edwin Arnaudin

reviews.text: It's flat-footed even when the setups yearn to be playful, like a pursuit that detours into a men-only bathhouse, or a surreal moment in an undercover sequence when Chastain rips off her red wig disguise to reveal ... her own identical red hair.
reviews.author: Amy Nicholson

reviews.text: The 355 is an unambitious action film, and no one involved did much to make it interesting.
reviews.author: Emily Wheeler

reviews.text: Even by the very, very low standards of early January action movies, "The 355" fails in its most basic tasks: repetitive and dull.
reviews.author: Nell Minow

reviews.text: Chastain, Kruger, Nyong'o, Cruz, and Fan infuse the movie with energy and enthusiasm.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: An international ensemble of A-list Hollywood actresses kick a whole lot of a**, but cannot save a spectacularly convoluted espionage actioner.
reviews.author: Julian Roman

reviews.text: While its action and story are just so-so, it has an enviable cast that might warrant a sequel based on their skills alone.
reviews.author: Alex Bentley

reviews.text: ... The story is nothing but formulaic situations used dozens of times before in dozens of films. The movie is so predictable that, from the outset, you are two or three steps ahead of the game.
reviews.author: Bob Bloom

reviews.text: Invite as many A-listers to your party as you can - but make sure they have something more substantial to eat than American cheese sandwiches served on Wonder bread with extra mayonnaise.
reviews.author: Sean O'Connell

reviews.text: As a spy movie, The 355 is as unrealistic as James Bond being a Russian astronaut becoming an American cowboy who starts working for the CIA ... This 'female empowerment' film [is] embarrassing to women [and] anyone who wants to make or see a good movie.
reviews.author: Carla Hay

reviews.text: The result is inoffensive and instantly forgettable, only noteworthy for putting together such an impressive ensemble cast
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: An action-packed but stiff spy story that gets the big showy set pieces right but doesn't invest enough in its characters.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: Despite a few scattered moments, the team-up action of "The 355" never fully comes together.
reviews.author: Mark Olsen

reviews.text: ... the gaps between (standard choreographed set destruction scenes) are filled with marshmallow fluff, such as the reluctance of any bad guy to kill the spy gals... because they're women, and it's very important to remind viewers of that...
reviews.author: Kevin A. Ranson

reviews.text: A year from now, you may see the DVD in Redbox and ask your spouse, 'Did we see that?' She (or he) will most likely shrug uncertainly.
reviews.author: Kenneth R. Morefield

reviews.text: The international affectations feel like pantomime-final concessions that might come from one of the disappointing G8 summits where despite having all that power in one room, the best they can do is agree to meet again next year.
reviews.author: David Crow

reviews.text: The 355 is the cinematic equivalent of Hydrox.
reviews.author: Josh Spiegel

reviews.text: Chastain leads a group of (mostly) strong women, whose power radiates throughout the film.
reviews.author: Allison Rose

reviews.text: The best, and really only thing to say about The 355 is that it's fine. Unremarkable in every way, this has been done much better and been done much worse.
reviews.author: Brent McKnight

reviews.text: Rather than fully capitalize on a film featuring an ensemble cast that could easily let out a wild side, here's a film that plays like another wannabe Bourne film.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: Five thrillingly charismatic performers, a giddy central premise and a single memorable one-liner can't save this hotchpotch production from its ruinous inadequacies.
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: The 355 never shakes off a sense of wasted talent and opportunity.
reviews.author: Kevin Harley

reviews.text: Those used to more complex espionage puzzles might feel a bit disappointed with the writing, but the performances, and their commitment to the story, keep the production on the move.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: Film is cliché in every way and lacking in style, but the ladies kick ass in a practical and realistic way that makes this spy thriller a guilty pleasure.
reviews.author: Lupe Rodriguez Haas

reviews.text: The real problem... is the script by Kinberg (who has written a lot of "X-Men" movies) and Theresa Rebeck.
reviews.author: Chris Hewitt

reviews.text: The chases, fights and fun bits of spy craft are brightly and pacily shot, but the 'twists' are barely surprising. These women, and these characters, deserve more.
reviews.author: Helen O'Hara

reviews.text: Despite a decent collection of leading ladies, this is one of the least clever spy flicks ever made.
reviews.author: Mike Massie

reviews.text: What had been slick emptiness in a diverting sort of way... becomes curdled slick emptiness in a look-at-your-watch sort of way.
reviews.author: Mark Feeney

reviews.text: Around the point where you'd be down to half-popped kernels and snack rubble, it raises the stakes and gets grittier and more compelling than you expected.
reviews.author: Leslie Felperin

reviews.text: Despite the keep-it-open ending, it seems clear that Chastain has an idea, and not a franchise; that Simon Kinberg (X-Men) works better as a producer than a director.
reviews.author: Fionnuala Halligan

reviews.text: Perhaps that's true equality in action - an international, diverse cast of actresses can now make a mediocre spy film...
reviews.author: Clarisse Loughrey

reviews.text: On screen, as in real life, simply dropping a woman into the same old role isn't enough to truly change the game.
reviews.author: Katie Rife

reviews.text: The cast might possess an enviable abundance of star quality, but "The 355" adds up to less than the sum of its parts.
reviews.author: Brian Lowry

reviews.text: I was pleasantly entertained watching these chicks wheel around and elbow men in the throat, especially Kruger, who obviously could kill me without breaking a sweat.
reviews.author: Johanna Schneller

reviews.text: "The 355" is a guilty pleasure, only don't waste time feeling guilty.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: Will we be talking about this movie in a few hundred years? Probably not. But in the here and now, these agents of destruction pack a lovely punch.
reviews.author: Charlotte O'Sullivan

reviews.text: The material might've gotten by with a different director...
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: The impulse to put kickass women in charge for a change is commendable, but the journeyman result suggests the pitfalls of starting with the packaging instead of the storytelling inspiration.
reviews.author: David Rooney

reviews.text: The first big release of the year doubling up as its first big disappointment.
reviews.author: Benjamin Lee

reviews.text: Starry, silly escapism with pop-feminist flare and a passport.
reviews.author: Leah Greenblatt

reviews.text: Mostly holds your attention, periodically revs the senses, and gives its actors just enough to work with to put a basic feminine spin on the genre.
reviews.author: Owen Gleiberman

reviews.text: While "The 355" might not be the boundary-busting breakthrough it was sold as, it's something better: a solid spy flick that adds something new to the genre without totally upending it.
reviews.author: Kate Erbland

reviews.text: It's the film equivalent of a high-fructose, corn-syrup-based fizzy drink being passed off as chic in taller, slimmer cans.
reviews.author: Robbie Collin

reviews.text: [The] screenplay only gives each of these actors the bare minimum with which to work. The plot reflects a similar attitude.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: ...The 355 just isn't a good film.
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: There are moments of intrigue and big-budget polish, but I'd wager the cast (and contractual obligations) is the only reason 'The 355' didn't get sold to a streamer or end up as a Lionsgate Premiere VOD title.
reviews.author: Scott Mendelson

reviews.text: A female-driven spy thriller, The 355 is a globetrotting adventure with an A-list cast and a Z-list script.
reviews.author: James Mottram

reviews.text: Even a collection of the most talented actresses can't elevate this tired, generic action movie to new heights.
reviews.author: EJ Moreno

reviews.text: The final results suggest that more effort went into crafting a top-flight ensemble than into giving these women characters to play or crafting a spy story that didn't hit all the obvious plot beats in all the obvious international locations.
reviews.author: Alonso Duralde

reviews.text: Despite an all-star cast, this tepid action adventure leaves a lot to be desired.
reviews.author: Evan Dossey

reviews.text: The type of bland spy action-thriller we've seen done so many times before, and mostly better.
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: Despite the cast's best efforts, the film stumbles out of the starting blocks and fails to pick itself up out of the inevitable sea of testosterone.
reviews.author: Katie Smith-Wong

reviews.text: The 355 feels as if it intended to set up a franchise, only to get discouraged before it reaches its first finish line.
reviews.author: Jesse Hassenger

reviews.text: The 355 is afraid to have fun with its story, but it should be embarrassed to take a rote formula so seriously.
reviews.author: Fred Topel

reviews.text: While the story doesn't add anything new or significant to the espionage genre, it's the thrill of the fast-paced action scenes and a charismatic ensemble that makes it worthwhile watching at least once.
reviews.author: Jamie Broadnax

reviews.text: The 355 is filled with generic tropes, lackluster action, and an uninspired story that'll leave audiences yawning not yearning for more.
reviews.author: Matt Rodriguez

reviews.text: The film treats its premise as the backdrop for a trite celebration of empowerment and teamwork among professional women.
reviews.author: Jake Cole

reviews.text: The film just about avoids female empowerment clichés to deliver as an enjoyably gritty and glamorous actioner.
reviews.author: Hanna Flint

synopsis: When a top-secret weapon falls into mercenary hands, wild card CIA agent Mason "Mace" Brown (Oscar®-nominated actress Jessica Chastain) will need to join forces with rival badass German agent Marie (Diane Kruger, In the Fade), former MI6 ally and cutting-edge computer specialist Khadijah (Oscar® winner Lupita Nyong'o), and skilled Colombian psychologist Graciela (Oscar® winner Penélope Cruz) on a lethal, breakneck mission to retrieve it, while also staying one-step ahead of a mysterious woman, Lin Mi Sheng (Bingbing Fan, X-Men: Days of Future Past), who is tracking their every move. As the action rockets around the globe from the cafes of Paris to the markets of Morocco to the opulent auction houses of Shanghai, the quartet of women will forge a tenuous loyalty that could protect the world--or get them killed.
